details: The immediately preceding definition permits finite p only when p>0 and gives no L0 definition; moreover q/p is undefined at p=0.
Thus the source-supported correction is 0<p≤q≤∞, or p≠0 when exponents inhabit a nonnegative extended domain.
q=∞ is explicitly part of the displayed range.
Its right-hand side means ess sup |X|.
The source's one-sentence Jensen justification does not itself cover q=∞, so that endpoint requires the essential-supremum argument or a limiting argument.
The norm is nondecreasing with the exponent: the smaller-exponent quantity is on the left.
Both quantities concern the same random variable on the same probability space.
The monotonicity claim includes 0<p<1 even though ‖·‖_{L^p} is not a norm there.

undebatable_constraints: Equation (1.3) has direction ‖X‖_{L^p}≤‖X‖_{L^q} for ordered exponents (PDF page 2, printed page 6).
A faithful corrected formulation must exclude p=0 because the source defines the finite-p expression only for p>0 and uses q/p in its justification (PDF pages 1-2, printed pages 5-6).
The correction must not discard q=∞, which is explicitly printed and separately defined through essential supremum (PDF pages 1-2, printed pages 5-6).
The claim is not restricted to p≥1; its corrected range includes every positive p, including p<1 (PDF page 2, printed page 6).
The absolute moment E|X|^p, not a signed moment, defines the quantity being compared (PDF page 1, printed page 5).
Probability-space normalization is part of the source context (PDF page 1, printed page 5).

contract_plain_english: For a real-valued random variable on a probability space, its Lp size cannot decrease as the exponent increases: if 0<p≤q≤∞, then ‖X‖_{L^p}≤‖X‖_{L^q}, with q=∞ interpreted as essential supremum. The book literally prints 0≤p, but p=0 conflicts with its own definition and with the ratio q/p, so the corrected claim requires a positive—or, in a nonnegative extended-exponent representation, nonzero—lower exponent. The infinity endpoint remains part of the claim even though it needs a separate essential-supremum justification.
